name: Foursquare Open Source Places (FSQ OS Places)
what_it_holds: Foursquare's open-sourced global places dataset (Apache 2.0 license), ~100M+ POI records (dataset docs cite up to ~1B rows counting historical/duplicate entries; ~239GB total across parquet files for places + a separate categories file). Commercial categories include hotels/lodging, restaurants, retail; 34 non-commercial categories (airports, cities, taxi stands, etc.) are flagged for filtering out. Distributed as Parquet on Hugging Face (gated download, free after accepting terms); no GitHub repo found for a companion access tool as of this check.
why_useful: Gap #20/#8/#9: a free, global, commercially-licensed (Apache 2.0) alternative POI census to build a worldwide hotel/lodging count by city and to identify non-Airbnb short-term-rental-adjacent venues (hostels, vacation rental offices) as a supply cross-check; could also proxy tourism-attraction density by market for demand normalization.
time_coverage: Single current snapshot (released 2024); unclear if historical snapshots are retained
themes: POI and place data: Overture Maps places, OSM extracts (tourism=*), Foursquare open places, Geofabrik tooling; counting STR/hotel supply from maps
why_all: Gap #20/#8/#9: a free, global, commercially-licensed (Apache 2.0) alternative POI census to build a worldwide hotel/lodging count by city and to identify non-Airbnb short-term-rental-adjacent venues (hostels, vacation rental offices) as a supply cross-check; could also proxy tourism-attraction density by market for demand normalization.

name: AiguaDeBarcelona_DataChallenge
what_it_holds: Barcelona water utility (Aigües de Barcelona) data-challenge repo: water consumption measured by meter, broken out by industrial / domestic / tourism-sector use, by geographical region within Barcelona, for 2019-2021 (pre/post-COVID span). Repo structure has db/, model/, src/, app.py (Flask), requirements.txt; described as analysing consumption 'by industrial, domestic and tourism factors using AI'. Apache-2.0 licensed. Exact row/column counts and CSV filenames not confirmed by the fetch (would need a clone to see db/ contents).
why_useful: Barcelona is one of our 13 held Inside Airbnb panel cities. A tourism-sector water-consumption series by district, spanning a COVID collapse and recovery, is a genuine independent occupancy proxy for a market we already track — directly on-theme for 'utility consumption as occupancy proxy' and could cross-check the Barcelona Inside Airbnb reviews-based stays index.
size_hint: unknown row count; multi-year meter-level utility data by sector/region
themes: Electricity, water and waste data as occupancy proxies (smart-meter open data, tourist-area utility consumption), and mobile-phone tourism statistics (Eurostat MNO experimental)
why_all: Barcelona is one of our 13 held Inside Airbnb panel cities. A tourism-sector water-consumption series by district, spanning a COVID collapse and recovery, is a genuine independent occupancy proxy for a market we already track — directly on-theme for 'utility consumption as occupancy proxy' and could cross-check the Barcelona Inside Airbnb reviews-based stays index.

name: Hurricanes_and_Migration
what_it_holds: Complete county-to-county migration flow matrices built from IRS-SOI data, 1998-2015, as CSVs in outflows/ and inflows/ folders (yearly matrices e.g. 0101in.csv, plus aggregated outflow.csv/inflow.csv). Also ships hurricanes.json: US federal disaster assistance records 1990-2018 with affected county FIPS, costs, casualties, dates. Python scripts analyze migration response to Katrina and Sandy.
why_useful: Long, clean, ready-to-use IRS migration panel (1998-2015) at county level -- can be extended/joined with post-2015 IRS SOI vintages to build a second-home / relocation proxy for STR demand in destination counties (sunbelt/vacation-market in-migration), and the hurricane-shock design is a template for isolating migration-driven demand shifts.
size_hint: ~18 annual matrix pairs + 2 aggregate CSVs + 1 JSON
themes: Population, migration and second-home data (IRS migration, Census CPS, USPS change of address, second-home counts, holiday-home shares Europe)
why_all: Long, clean, ready-to-use IRS migration panel (1998-2015) at county level -- can be extended/joined with post-2015 IRS SOI vintages to build a second-home / relocation proxy for STR demand in destination counties (sunbelt/vacation-market in-migration), and the hurricane-shock design is a template for isolating migration-driven demand shifts.

Longer span than the mathewhauer repo (through 2015) and pairs migration directly with hurricane/disaster shocks by county — directly useful for gap 11 (events/shocks, hurricanes) and for modeling population/second-home exposure to storm-affected STR markets (Florida, Gulf Coast, coastal Northeast).

name: blackmarbler
what_it_holds: R package (World Bank DIME) that automates downloading and processing NASA Black Marble (VIIRS-derived) daily/monthly/annual nighttime-lights composites from NASA LAADS DAAC and aggregating radiance to any user-defined WGS84 polygon. No committed raw data (requires free NASA bearer token); demonstrated with 2012-2022+ near-real-time data (daily lag ~1 week). Actively maintained World Bank org repo.
why_useful: Same use case as blackmarblepy for teams working in R; redundant capability, listed for completeness.
themes: Occupancy/demand estimation from satellite, nightlights, or imagery; parking-lot counts; Sentinel-based tourism activity
why_all: Same use case as blackmarblepy for teams working in R; redundant capability, listed for completeness.

One-command, point-in-time-capable pull of nightlights for any Airbnb market polygon (city/region) as a tourism/economic-activity proxy at monthly or even daily granularity, addressing gap #5 (engagement/activity proxies) and the broader satellite-tourism-activity theme; because it hits NASA's archive directly it could be re-run vintage-by-vintage for point-in-time construction.

name: stalker-challenge
what_it_holds: A solved take-home 'Stalker Challenge' from AllTheRooms (an STR analytics vendor named explicitly in our gap #2). Repo is a single Jupyter notebook (StalkerChallenge.ipynb); the original challenge dataset lives at alltherooms.github.io and was not independently verified as still live in this pass -- needs a follow-up fetch of that link and the notebook contents to confirm what STR fields (ADR, occupancy, listing counts) the challenge dataset actually contains and for which market/year.
why_useful: Not an STR-vendor dataset at all, but the Gowalla check-in dataset it points to is directly named in CONTEXT.md gap #20 (geotagged tourism/check-in datasets for party-size/group-travel/cross-border proxies) -- worth noting as a rediscovery path to that Stanford dataset via a real-estate-tech hiring challenge, and evidence AllTheRooms itself does not expose free market data even for recruiting purposes.
size_hint: Gowalla external dataset: ~6.4M check-ins (per SNAP listing, not re-verified here)
themes: AirDNA / Mashvisor / AllTheRooms / Transparent / Key Data / Rabbu / Awning sample exports or scraped market pages committed to GitHub
Alternative-data vendor sample repos: vendors publishing free samples on GitHub (Advan, Similarweb, Apptopia, Yipit-like, Consumer Edge, Earnest, M Science, Quiver Quant, Thinknum)
why_all: Not an STR-vendor dataset at all, but the Gowalla check-in dataset it points to is directly named in CONTEXT.md gap #20 (geotagged tourism/check-in datasets for party-size/group-travel/cross-border proxies) -- worth noting as a rediscovery path to that Stanford dataset via a real-estate-tech hiring challenge, and evidence AllTheRooms itself does not expose free market data even for recruiting purposes.

AllTheRooms is one of the named realised-ADR/occupancy vendors we are missing (gap #2); a public hiring-challenge dataset from them, even a toy sample, could hint at their schema or, if the full challenge dataset is still hosted, provide an actual small STR panel with real ADR/occupancy for at least one market.
